:::{#def-relative-efficiency}
#### Relative efficiency

Let $\hparam_a$ and $\hparam_b$ be two estimators of the same estimand $\param$.
The **relative efficiency** of $\hparam_a$ with respect to $\hparam_b$
is the ratio of their [mean squared errors](estimation.qmd#def-mse),
the less accurate estimator's in the numerator:

$$\frac{\mselr{\hparam_b}}{\mselr{\hparam_a}}$$

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

@CaseBerg01 [sec. 7.3.1].
:::

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-relative-efficiency}
#### Reading the relative efficiency

A relative efficiency above 1 means $\hparam_a$ is more accurate than $\hparam_b$,
and below 1 means it is less accurate.
For two [unbiased](estimation.qmd#def-unbiased) estimators the mean squared errors are the variances
([mean squared error equals bias squared plus variance](estimation.qmd#thm-mse-bias-variance), with zero bias),
so the relative efficiency is the ratio of the variances.
:::
